rules_served: DT-* (the DTI's rental treatment, LP-642 step 3)
summary_hint: Small Residential Income Property Appraisal Report (Fannie Form 1025 / Freddie 72) — the appraiser's opinion of monthly market rent for a two- to four-unit property, with the comparable rentals supporting it.

typed_core.name: form_type
typed_core.why: the form itself states 1007 or 1025; the unit count is a separate field and must not be used to infer it

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: matches the schedule's subject to the loan's subject (LP-642 step 3)

typed_core.name: opinion_of_monthly_market_rent
typed_core.why: THE FIGURE THE DTI CONSUMES. The appraiser's opinion of monthly market rent for the SUBJECT AS A WHOLE. Printed differently on the two forms and labelled 'Opinion of Monthly Market Rent' on NEITHER: on a 1007 it is the foot-of-page sentence 'I (WE) ESTIMATE THE MONTHLY MARKET RENT OF THE SUBJECT AS OF ___ TO BE $ ___'; on a 1025 there is no property-level opinion line at all — 'Opinion Of Market Rent' is a per-UNIT column heading, and the property-level figure is the printed 'Total Gross Monthly Rent'. Taking a single unit's row on a four-unit subject would qualify the loan on a quarter of its rent.

typed_core.name: total_gross_monthly_income
typed_core.why: 1025 only: the form's 'Total Estimated Monthly Income' — Total Gross Monthly Rent PLUS 'Other Monthly Income (itemize)' (parking, laundry, storage). NOT the qualifying rent and NOT interchangeable with the opinion: substituting it would put non-rent income into a qualifying ratio. Captured so a reader can see what other income the appraiser recorded. Null on a 1007.

typed_core.name: unit_count
typed_core.why: 1 on a 1007, 2-4 on a 1025; decides which form is required (B3-3.8-02)

typed_core.name: effective_date
typed_core.why: B3-3.8-01 ages the form against the note date

typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: processor — ties the form to the file

nested_lists.name: comparable_rentals
nested_lists.shape_reason: the grid is the EVIDENCE behind the opinion and genuinely repeats (3+ comparables). Values are kept VERBATIM as strings — a rent written '$1,850/mo' and an adjustment '-100' are what the appraiser wrote, and the DTI consumes the opinion rather than the grid, so normalising here would lose fidelity for no gain.

nested_lists.name: unit_rents
nested_lists.shape_reason: a 1025 breaks rent down per unit and a 1007 does not; empty on a 1007. ACTUAL and MARKET rent are distinct columns and are kept in separate fields — merging them would lose the difference between what a tenant pays and what the market supports.

rejected.name: comparable_photographs
rejected.reason: images, not data; the catch-all keeps any caption text

rejected.name: averaged_comparable_rent
rejected.reason: COMPUTED, and computing it would invite the model to substitute it for the opinion — the exact failure the prompt forbids. An appraiser's opinion is a judgement, not the mean of the rows above it.

rejected.name: per_unit_opinion_of_market_rent
rejected.reason: A 1025's 'Opinion Of Market Rent' column is per UNIT and has no single-field home: rows 1-4 are captured in `unit_rents` and the property-level figure is the form's printed 'Total Gross Monthly Rent', which is what `opinion_of_monthly_market_rent` holds. A scalar for the per-unit opinion would invite exactly the substitution the prompt forbids.

encoding_variations: Joint branding: 'Freddie Mac Form 1000' IS the Fannie 1007, and 'Freddie Mac Form 72' IS the 1025. A model reading the Freddie number off the header has no way to know which Fannie form it holds unless told, so the prompt maps both.

The two forms state the property-level market rent in structurally different places — a sentence on the 1007, a printed total on the 1025 — and neither prints the words 'Opinion of Monthly Market Rent' as a line label.

A tenanted subject shows an ACTUAL rent alongside the market opinion; only the opinion qualifies income. On a 1025 that is 'Total Actual Monthly Rent'; on a 1007 it is 'Monthly Rental If Currently Rented' in the subject column.

open_questions.question: Should a 1004 URAR carrying a rent addendum map to this type or stay separate?
open_questions.why_not_blocking: No real URAR-with-addendum was available. The extractor reads a 1007/1025 and the prompt tells it to null every field on anything else, so a URAR is refused rather than mis-mapped — safe until one is seen.

notes: LP-642 step 2/3. Field names checked against the real blank forms — Freddie Mac Form 1000 / Fannie Mae Form 1007 (8/88) and Fannie Mae Form 1025 / Freddie Mac Form 72 (03/2005).
BLANK forms, so this is the PRINTED field vocabulary, not what an appraiser writes into the boxes. Accuracy against completed forms is still unvalidated.
B3-3.8-02 (09/02/2026) makes one of these mandatory where rental income qualifies the loan.
